newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian coffee shipments delayed by strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee shipments delayed by strike.

text.p: A strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union could delay exports of up to 200,000 70-kg bags of coffee this week and may cause serious problems meeting May export commitments, a leading industry official said.

"There's an important quantity of coffee that's being held up. Over the course of this week, the buildup could easily be to the order of 100,000 to 200,000 bags," Diego Arango Mora, a member of the National Coffee Growers' Committee, told Reuters.

He said the figure was based on average weekly shipments by private exporters and National Coffee Growers' Federation alike. The federation has said Colombia was due to ship 900,000 70-kg bags in April.

A nationwide strike by the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) began at midnight Saturday. Arango Mora, who spoke by telephone from the central coffee-growing province of Quindio, said May export schedules would definitely be affected if the work stoppage extended beyond this week.
Some export comitments were already being affected, he added, saying the situation varied from one exporter to the next, depending on their individual contracts with roasters abroad.
